hints.title: Full Sort Overhead
hints.text: Sorting the entire list of frequencies costs O(U log U) where U is the count of distinct elements. When you only need the k largest entries, do you need to sort the whole collection?

hints.title: Bounded Selection Structure
hints.text: Count frequencies first, then maintain only the k most frequent items using a bounded selection structure or bucket frequencies from 1 to N.

hints.title: Frequency Count and Min-Heap
hints.text: Count occurrences of each number. Place elements into buckets indexed by frequency or push them through a min-priority structure capped at size k. Finally, collect the top k elements from the highest frequencies.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
K: target number of frequent elements (1 <= k <= distinct elements)
complexity.notes: Frequency counting takes O(N). Maintaining a min-heap of size K takes O(U log K) where U <= N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting all U unique elements takes O(U log U) time. For N = 10^5 distinct elements, sorting is slower than maintaining a size-k heap (O(N log K)) or bucket sort (O(N)).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining a heap of size K keeps extra heap space bounded by O(K), offering predictable cache performance over full array sorting.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Counting frequencies first, using min-heap of size K (not max-heap of size N), discussing O(N) bucket sort alternative, and verifying K <= number of unique elements.

solutions.approach: Frequency Counter + Min-Heap of Size K
Priority Queue Min-Heap of Size K
